rationale:
Numeric and boolean values in an agent's step config never reach the action they are meant to configure, fleet-wide. ExtractActionInputs (platform/orchestration/datahelpers/action_inputs.go) reads step config in four places and every one of them asserts config[field].(string) — and even then treats the resulting string as a REFERENCE to resolve against collectedData, never as a literal value. A JSON number fails the type assertion outright, so nothing lands in result.Values and the action falls through to whatever Go fallback its call site passes. The DB is the documented tuning surface for these actions, so the practical effect is that an operator changes a number, observes no change, and reasonably concludes the number was already correct.

This went unnoticed because the seeded value equalled the code default. content-feed-orchestrator's render_news_json step config carries max_age_hours 72; RenderNewsSectionAction calls inputs.GetInt("max_age_hours", 72). Config and behaviour agreed, so the config looked live and load-bearing while being decorative. max_items 6 in the same config has likewise never been read — it merely equals its own fallback.

Established by prediction rather than by reading code alone. vetcomparison.uk has two CMA feed items ~483h old. Setting the live config to 720 (30 days) must include them and 72 must not. The run carried 720 in its own initial_request_data.agent_config; the renderer's query run verbatim against the live DB with 720 returns both items; the run nevertheless produced item_count 0 and items [] — exactly what a 72h window predicts. check_has_news then routed 0 -> complete, skipping commit_news, so data/latest-news.json was never published and the homepage component renders a headline over nothing. The deployed binary was confirmed to contain the current query by checking the running pod (strings /app/agent-chassis | grep -c loadNewsItems -> 5), not git.

The fix adds a final strategy that takes a config value as a literal when it is a non-string scalar. It is deliberately restricted to non-strings. References are always strings, so this cannot alter how any existing reference resolves; it only fills fields that are currently being dropped on the floor. A string that fails to resolve is deliberately left absent rather than taken as its own value, because turning a broken reference into a silent literal would mask real wiring bugs — that is a separate and riskier change, and there is a live case of it (DirectoryExportAction aborting on an empty domain) filed separately as correlation 55dc0fa4-116c-40d6-90b2-bfad9ad73692.

The change runs last, so any value resolved by an earlier strategy still wins; it only fills gaps. Full case file: bugs_open/042.

plan.summary: Numeric and boolean values in agent step config never reach the actions they configure, fleet-wide: every config-reading branch of ExtractActionInputs asserts config[field].(string) and treats the result as a reference to resolve against collectedData, so a JSON number fails the type assertion and the action silently falls through to its Go fallback. This adds a final strategy taking non-string SCALAR config values as literals, restricted so it cannot alter how any existing string reference resolves.

edits.rationale: Add Strategy 5, after all reference-resolution strategies and before required-field validation, taking non-string scalar config values as literals. Restricted by an explicit type switch to bool, the sized/unsized int and uint families, float32/float64 and json.Number. Composite values (objects, arrays) are excluded because there is no evidence they were ever intended as literals here. It only fills fields still unset, so an earlier-resolved value always wins. Requires adding encoding/json to the import block for the json.Number case.

Regression cover for the defect and, just as importantly, for the behaviours deliberately preserved. Every test uses a configured value that DIFFERS from the fallback, because the defect hid precisely because a seeded value matched its default — a test reusing the default would pass either way and prove nothing.
edits.sketch:
TestExtractActionInputs_NumericConfigLiteralReachesAction — config max_age_hours 720 with GetInt fallback 72 must yield 720.
TestExtractActionInputs_IntAndJSONNumberAndBoolLiterals — plain int, json.Number and bool literals all carried.
TestExtractActionInputs_StringReferencesStillResolve — dot-path and single-segment string references still resolve from collectedData (the behaviour the config format depends on).
TestExtractActionInputs_UnresolvedStringIsNotTakenAsLiteral — an unresolvable string stays ABSENT, so a broken reference stays visible.
TestExtractActionInputs_ResolvedValueWinsOverLiteral — a value resolved from collectedData beats the config literal; Strategy 5 only fills gaps.

platform/orchestration/datahelpers/action_inputs.go:62 — `if v, ok := ai.Values[key].(float64); ok { return int(v) }` — GetInt already handles the float64 that JSON numbers unmarshal to, so no conversion work is needed once the value lands
platform/orchestration/actions/render_news_section_action.go:119 — `maxAgeHours := inputs.GetInt("max_age_hours", 72)` — the fallback that silently wins

plan.risks: Blast radius is every action that reads step config, so the restriction is the safety argument. Strategy 5 runs LAST and only fills fields still unset, so any value resolved by an earlier strategy still wins (covered by TestExtractActionInputs_ResolvedValueWinsOverLiteral). It is restricted to non-string scalars: references are always strings, so no existing reference resolution can change (covered by TestExtractActionInputs_StringReferencesStillResolve). Composite values (objects/arrays) are excluded deliberately. An unresolvable string is still left ABSENT rather than taken literally, so a broken reference stays visible instead of silently becoming a literal (covered by TestExtractActionInputs_UnresolvedStringIsNotTakenAsLiteral). What a reviewer should check: whether any action currently RELIES on a numeric config key being ignored — i.e. somewhere the seeded number differs from the Go fallback and the fallback is the value actually wanted. That is the one way this change alters live behaviour, and it would do so by making the config authoritative, which is the documented intent. Go change, inert until the next image roll.
